entries.topicDescription: Structuring a multi-module Android project: module boundaries, dependencies, and build performance.

tips.title: Modularization speeds up builds by letting Gradle skip unaffected modules
tips.content:
In a single-module app, any code change forces Gradle to recompile the
entire codebase, since there's no smaller unit of compilation to isolate
the change to.

Splitting the app into well-bounded modules lets Gradle's incremental
build and configuration cache skip recompiling modules whose inputs
haven't changed — a change confined to a `:feature:profile` module
doesn't force a rebuild of `:feature:checkout` or `:core:network`,
significantly speeding up iterative local builds on a large codebase.
